final_answer:
## Short answer

**Two things are competing for "most recent," depending on what counts as a macOS security update:**

| Release | Date | Available for |
|---|---|---|
| **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2** — most recent macOS *OS* update | 17 Aug 2026 | macOS Tahoe only |
| **Safari 26.6.1** — most recent security release *affecting macOS* | 18 Aug 2026 | macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia |

**Apple identifies no actively exploited issues in either one.** ([Apple security releases](https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100))

---

## macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 (17 Aug 2026)

- Every entry on the advisory carries the line "Available for: macOS Tahoe" — so this update targets Tahoe only. Sequoia and Sonoma did **not** get a same-day OS counterpart; their most recent OS updates remain 15.7.9 and 14.8.9 from 6 Aug ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281), [release list](https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100)).
- It fixes roughly 30 CVEs, the largest cluster (~18) in WebKit, plus ImageIO (CVE-2026-65346, integer overflow → arbitrary code execution), IOGPUFamily (CVE-2026-64788), and Kernel issues CVE-2026-65343 (use-after-free) and CVE-2026-65349 (out-of-bounds read). *Caveat: I read this advisory through a page-summarizing fetch rather than transcribing it line by line, so treat the exact count and the completeness of this CVE list as approximate — the advisory itself is authoritative* ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281)).
- **The page contains no "exploited," "exploitation," or "Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited" language** — Apple's standard formula for in-the-wild attacks is absent ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281)).

## The actively exploited issue — and why it is *not* Apple identifying it

There **is** an actively exploited macOS flaw right now, but the exploitation finding does not come from Apple:

- **CVE-2026-65400**, Screen Sharing: "An attacker on the network may be able to authenticate to Screen Sharing without valid credentials." Fixed via improved state management; credited to Alfredo Pesoli (@\_\_rev) via Bynario Atlas. Patched **6 Aug 2026** in **macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, and macOS Sonoma 14.8.9** ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148170)).
- Apple's advisory for it **also carries no exploitation notice** ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148170)).
- Exploitation was reported externally: NCSC-NL warned on 12 Aug that attackers are hitting Macs with port 5900 exposed to the internet, gaining root and installing a Monero miner; CISA rescored the bug from 7.1 to 9.8 on 14 Aug and added it to the KEV catalog on 18 Aug with a 21 Aug federal remediation deadline ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/apple-macos-screen-sharing-flaw.html), [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/08/17/apple-macos-screen-sharing-flaw/), [Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/cyber-security/macos-screen-sharing-flaw-exploited-to-root-macs-and-plant-monero-miners), [Malwarebytes](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/bugs/2026/08/update-your-mac-screen-sharing-vulnerability-exploited-in-the-wild)).

So the precise answer to your question as asked: **Apple identifies zero actively exploited issues in its most recent macOS security update.** The one macOS vulnerability known to be under attack was already patched eleven days earlier, and its exploited status was established by NCSC-NL and CISA rather than by Apple.

## Fact vs. inference vs. uncertainty

- **Supported fact:** release dates, "Available for" scoping, CVE-2026-65400's description and credit, absence of exploitation language on Apple's pages, KEV addition.
- **Inference (mine):** that Sequoia/Sonoma were deliberately left at 15.7.9/14.8.9 for the 26.6.2 content — I infer this from the release list showing no 17 Aug counterpart for them; Apple does not explain the split, and one could still ship later.
- **Disagreement in sources:** the CVSS score for CVE-2026-65400 moved 7.1 → 9.8; that is a CISA rescoring, not two sources contradicting each other, but you'll see both numbers in circulation ([Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/cyber-security/macos-screen-sharing-flaw-exploited-to-root-macs-and-plant-monero-miners)). One secondary write-up characterizes the flaw as pre-auth **remote root code execution** via a Secure Remote Password implementation bug, which is stronger than Apple's own wording of "authenticate without valid credentials" ([Huntress](https://www.huntress.com/blog/macos-screen-sharing-rce-patched)).
- **Weak evidence:** a related second Screen Sharing CVE (CVE-2026-43760) appears in third-party analysis; I did not verify it against an Apple advisory, so don't rely on it.
- **Not established:** whether Apple will retroactively annotate advisory 148170 with an exploitation note, as it has done occasionally in the past. As of today it has not.

**Practical upshot:** Tahoe users should be on 26.6.2; Sequoia/Sonoma users need 15.7.9 / 14.8.9 for the exploited Screen Sharing bug plus Safari 26.6.1. If Screen Sharing/VNC (port 5900) is reachable from the internet on any unpatched Mac, treat that as urgent.
